chunks: From him, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Mansurrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:
"When the coating (of impurity) exceeds one-third by an Uqiyyah, it is Haram (impure)."

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةً: An Uqiyyah (a specific unit of weight)
key_terms.الطِّلاَءُ: The coating or layer of impurity (najāsah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on clothing with impurity covering more than one-third?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific quantitative threshold for ritual impurity (*najāsah*) on clothing, establishing that if the impure area exceeds one-third by the weight of an *Uqiyyah*, the entire garment is considered impure. This ruling is crucial for Shia jurisprudence (*fiqh*) regarding the validity of prayer (*ṣalāh*), as it provides a precise metric for determining when an item transitions from being partially impure to wholly impure, thereby invalidating the prayer if not purified.
